correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite commutative chain ring R with residue q and length ell, the commutator of triangular 2-by-2 matrices is exactly the determinant of their nonscalar coordinate vectors. The primitive 2-by-k determinant-zero matrices over a chain quotient have a unit pivot and a primitive outer-product factorization; counting primitive factors modulo the unit group gives (q+1)(q^k-1)q^((k+1)(m-1)). Valuation shells t<ceil(ell/2) lift from length ell-2t with q^(2kt) choices; the deep shell has q^(2k floor(ell/2)) entries. Odd/even geometric sums yield D_{ell,k}=S_ell(q)q^(ell*k)-(S_ell(q)-1)q^((ell-1)k), hence C_k=S_ell(q)q^(2ell*k)-(S_ell(q)-1)q^((2ell-1)k). At k=0 the formula is 1. Stirling inversion produces the full distinct-clique polynomial; removal of q^ell universal scalar vertices gives the noncentral polynomial. Independent direct determinant enumeration for Z/4Z gave 25,600 ordered commuting triples, and Z/4Z pairs give 1,408; both match. Full proofs, not these finite checks, cover all q,ell,k.
